headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: both agents can write or act on shared outputs, while the uploader can push content to broad network destinations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read/write filesystem and its skills reference each other via shared context; B runs in CLI headless mode and can consume files like videos/images. If A’s outputs are placed in a shared workspace, B may ingest them as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is plausible, but not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or copied files are fed from A into B
IF B parses A-produced text or metadata as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct directories
Add a manual review step before B consumes any A output
Prefix A outputs with non-executable delimiters
Disable automatic file pickup between the agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing and product-marketing context and can write files; B handles account data and has broad network egress. If the pair shares files or credentials, A can stage sensitive content that B may upload through its outbound APIs. The exact shared-storage path is not documented, so the safer medium severity is chosen.
conditions: IF A writes marketing or product context into files that B later reads
IF B uploads content derived from shared files or account data over broad egress
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Store secrets outside any shared directory
Review B upload targets before execution
Redact sensitive fields from A outputs before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while B can also operate on files and has multiple instances with account-file session scope. Even though B cannot write files or modify git state, the pair still has overlapping mutable workspace pressure and concurrency risk. Because the shared-dir assumption is plausible but not proven, uncertainty is escalated to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or on the same account file
IF A and B run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory
Serialize access to shared files
Use per-account file locks for B
Avoid concurrent launches of multiple instances
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces marketing content and shared context, and B’s workflow is an auto-upload pipeline with broad network egress. If B treats A-generated artifacts as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into published uploads or account actions. This interaction is not directly documented, so the higher severity is chosen because the downstream blast radius can be public and hard to reverse.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced copy, captions, or metadata without verification
IF B uploads or publishes content derived from A outputs
mitigations: Require human approval before upload
Add a verification checklist for A outputs
Compare A outputs against source material
Limit B to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add content validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: A handles marketing and product-marketing context, while B handles account data and uploads to external platforms. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, but the combination creates a plausible compliance mismatch around account-data handling and logging. Because the exact policy gap is undocumented, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF account data or regulated customer content is routed through B
IF A-generated content includes personal or confidential information
mitigations: Minimize personal data in shared inputs
Review retention settings for both agents
Keep account secrets out of A outputs
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
